data.summary: The pod startup was delayed primarily by the readiness probe's initialDelaySeconds configuration, which forced a 90-second wait despite the application being ready in under 6 seconds. This conservative configuration is the sole cause of the SLO breach, as the application itself initialized quickly.

findings.statement: The application completed its initialization in 0.789 s, well within the 10 s SLO.
The readiness probe configuration includes an initialDelaySeconds of 90 s, which accounts for the 92.571 s duration of the readiness phase.

ruled_out.reason: The image pull completed in only 4.094 s for a 53 MB image, indicating normal pull performance.
Application initialization was fast, taking only 0.789 s.
Scheduling took 0 s, indicating no resource or capacity constraints during the scheduling phase.

recommendations.action: Reduce initialDelaySeconds in the readiness probe configuration.
recommendations.rationale: The current 90 s delay is significantly longer than the actual application startup time of approximately 5.4 s, causing unnecessary delays in pod readiness.
A startup probe would allow the application to signal readiness as soon as it is finished, while still protecting against slow starts without requiring a long, fixed initial delay.
